"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:3200 -- a "have / when" token detector.

What it does: this component fires on the word "have" (and "has", "having"), on
"when", and on the Chinese word 有 ("have"), which is what the model is most
sensitive to here. The activation is roughly constant on those tokens, so the
program predicts a fixed value per token class and nothing else:
  - " have", " having", " Have", "have" ...      -> 0.75
  - " when", " When", "When", "whenever", 当, 當  -> 0.75
  - " has", "has"                              -> 0.63
  - any token containing 有 (有, 具有, 也有 ...)  -> 0.60
  - a small set of entertainment / wrestling /
    celebrity nouns (fans, actor, cast, WWE ...)  -> 0.40
  - everything else                             -> 0.0

Why: the largest share of the variance is the "have/has/when" tokens; the
entertainment words add a little. Context (the subject before "have") changes the
value only slightly, so it is ignored. Predicting 0 elsewhere matches the
component's small background activity, which is noise spread over many tokens.
"""
READS = ()

HAVE = {" have", " Have", "have", " having", " Having", "having", " Has", "Having"}
HAS = {" has", "has"}
WHEN = {" when", " When", "When", "when", " whenever", "当", "當", "когда"}
SHOW = {
    " fans", " fan", " Fans", " actor", " actress", " cast", " celebrity",
    " wrestlers", " wrestler", " WWE", " wrestling", " Wrestle", " Hollywood",
    " viewers", " viewer", " starring", " filming", " premiere", " Netflix",
    " MTV", " debut", " producer", " film", " filmmakers", " IMDb", " Entertainment",
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if tok in HAVE or tok in WHEN:
        return None, 0.75
    if tok in HAS:
        return None, 0.63
    if "有" in tok:
        return None, 0.6
    if tok in SHOW:
        return None, 0.4
    return None, 0.0

    value = CHINESE_ACTIONS.get(token.strip(), value)
    value = OTHER_ACTIONS.get(token.strip(), value)

    # Reassemble only the current Latin word, not the entire text prefix.
    match = re.search(r'[A-Za-z]+$', token)
    current = match.group().lower() if match else ''
    if match and match.start() == 0:
        current = previous + current
    family = perform_word(current)
    if family in PERFORM:
        value = PERFORM[family]
        # Split endings have different strengths from an unsplit word.
        value = {'forming': 8.5, 'formed': 6.0, 'forms': 6.0,
                 'ing': 5.6}.get(word, value)
        if token.startswith('-') and family == 'performance':
            value = 5.7

        value = BOUND_FORMS.get(word.lstrip('-'), value)

    # Familiar constructions which continue the action/performance phrase.
    if token[:1].isspace():
        prev = perform_word(previous)
        if word == 'of' and prev in ('performance', 'performances'):
            value = 2.4
        elif word == 'out' and previous in ('carry', 'carried', 'carrying'):
            value = 1.2

            value = {'the': 1.4, 'a': 1.1, 'an': 0.8, 'this': 1.2}.get(
                word, value)

            not token.startswith(' ') or token.strip()[0].isupper()):
        value *= 0.5

weak responses to unrelated vocabulary.

    'context_dependent_physics': (0.27, 0.74, 0.0,

    'cjk_light_and_waves': (0.76, 0.60, 1.0,
        "光 阳光 光线 光源 激光 发光 照明 谱 射 反射 折射 辐射 電視 共振 频率 信号 光芒 光纤",

    'wave_measurements_and_roots': (0.56, 0.27, 0.4,
        "hz nm ghz mhz khz db watt dose dosimetry radi phot photoc ultr ampl "
        "intens spect",
        ""),
}

         for word in values[3].split()}
ROOTS = [(root, family) for family, values in FAMILIES.items()
         for root in values[4].split()]
LETTERS = re.compile(r"[^\W\d_]+", re.UNICODE)
TAIL = re.compile(r"[^\W\d_]+$", re.UNICODE)


def family_of(word):
    word = word.lower().lstrip('_-')
    if word in WORDS:
        return WORDS[word]
    for root, family in ROOTS:
        if word.startswith(root):
            return family
    # Ordinary English plurals, only when the singular is recognized.
    candidates = []
    if word.endswith('ies'):
        candidates.append(word[:-3] + 'y')
    if word.endswith('es'):
        candidates.append(word[:-2])
    if word.endswith('s'):
        candidates.append(word[:-1])
    for singular in candidates:
        if singular in WORDS:
            return WORDS[singular]
    return None


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        topic, previous_word = 0.0, ''
    else:
        _, topic, previous_word = carry
    topic *= 0.98
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = s.strip()
    family = family_of(word)
    continued = False
    head = LETTERS.match(s)
    if head and previous_word:
        combined = previous_word + head.group().lower()
        combined_family = family_of(combined)
        if combined_family:
            family = combined_family
            continued = True
    else:
        combined = word.lower()
    tail = TAIL.search(s)
    if head and head.end() == len(s) and previous_word:
        next_word = combined[-40:]
    else:
        next_word = tail.group().lower()[-40:] if tail else ''

    value = 0.0
    cue = 0.0
    if family:
        baseline, sensitivity, cue, _, _ = FAMILIES[family]
        value = baseline + sensitivity * min(topic, 3.0)
        if word and word[0].isupper():
            value -= 0.20
        if s and not s[0].isspace() and word.lstrip('_-').isascii():
            value -= 0.25
        if continued:
            cue = 0.0  # Do not count a single split word twice.
    topic = min(4.0, topic + cue)
    return (doc, topic, next_word), float(value)
programs.haiku:
"""Optics, waves and signals.

This component fires on words from physics and engineering about light, other
electromagnetic waves, lasers and lenses, spectra, radiation, radio, sound and signal
transmission (e.g. "light", "beam", "wavelength", "photon", "lens", "spectrum",
"radiation", "signal", "frequency", "radio", "sound", "speaker"). The strongest
response is to the optics words. A word counts on the token where it first reaches
its listed stem, so words split into several subword tokens (e.g. "ampl" + "ifier")
still count. The response grows when the passage is already about light or waves:
each earlier optics or wave word in the same document adds 20% (up to 5 of them)."""

READS = ()

# Optics: light and its instruments, and the physics of light.
OPTICS = ("light", "optic", "photon", "laser", "lens", "beam", "mirror", "prism",
          "telescop", "microscop", "scop", "reflect", "refract", "diffract", "absorb",
          "attenuat", "scatter", "transmi", "emit", "emission", "irradi", "illumin",
          "spectr", "spect", "radiat", "radi", "ray", "wavelength", "infrared",
          "ultraviolet", "focal", "focus", "intens", "polariz", "interfer", "dispers",
          "lumin", "brightness", "ultr")
# Waves, signals and radio/sound/electronics.
WAVES = ("wave", "speaker", "frequen", "signal", "radio", "antenna", "sound", "acoust", "ultrason",
         "amplitude", "amplif", "modulat", "oscill", "resonan", "electromagnet", "magnetic",
         "pulse", "broadcast", "audio", "video", "television", "tv")
# Devices and quantities that often sit near such words.
DEVICES = ("electric", "magnet", "energy", "dose", "image", "pixel",
           "microphone", "transmitter", "receiver", "detect", "sensor", "display", "camera",
           "watt", "hz", "nm", "source", "field", "power", "resolution", "filter", "polar",
           "heat", "vision", "color")
CJK = ("光", "波", "声", "訊", "放大", "谱", "辐射", "視")

def _level(word):
    if any(s in word for s in CJK) or word.startswith(OPTICS):
        return 0.83
    if word.startswith(WAVES):
        return 0.56
    if word.startswith(DEVICES):
        return 0.34
    return 0.0

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc, word, alpha, prev, hits = carry if carry is not None else (None, "", False, 0.0, 0)
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != doc:
        doc, word, alpha, prev, hits = prefix.document_ids[-1], "", False, 0.0, 0
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    letters = "".join(c for c in s.lower() if c.isalpha())
    cont = s[:1].isalpha() and alpha
    word = word + letters if cont else letters
    prev = prev if cont else 0.0
    alpha = s[-1:].isalpha()
    lvl = _level(word)
    new = lvl if lvl > prev else 0.0
    v = new * (1.0 + 0.2 * min(hits, 5))
    if new >= 0.8:
        hits += 1
    return (doc, word, alpha, max(prev, lvl), hits), v

"""Recognize text about light and other physical signals.

Optical words are the strongest cue; sound/electronics words get a smaller
prediction, and broad physical terms only a trace. Generic terms such as
'source' count when a nearby cue puts them in that topic.
"""
import re

READS = ()

OPTICS = (
    "light", "beam", "laser", "optic", "photon", "wavelength", "reflect",
    "spectr", "focal", "ray",
    "mirror", "emitter", "detector", "infrared", "ultraviolet", "radiation",
    "spectrum", "lens", "prism", "refraction", "fluorescen", "telescope",
    "sunlight", "illumina", "photodiode", "photomultiplier",
)
SOUND_SIGNAL = (
    "sound", "acoustic", "audio", "speaker", "frequency", "signal", "wave",
    "radio", "vibration", "transmit", "amplifier", "microphone", "voice",
)
BROAD_PHYSICS = (
    "electric", "voltage", "current", "energy", "power", "heat", "thermal",
    "television", "screen", "image", "video", "lamp", "bright", "solar",
)
AMBIGUOUS = ("source", "output", "emission", "absor", "incident", "attenuat",
             "transmission", "band", "field", "camera")
CJK_LIGHT_SOUND = set("光声波音電波")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        tail = ""
    else:
        tail = carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = (tail + token)[-180:]
    word_match = re.search(r"[a-z]+$", text.lower())
    word = word_match.group(0) if word_match else ""

    if any(ch in token for ch in CJK_LIGHT_SOUND):
        value = 0.5
    elif any(word.startswith(stem) for stem in OPTICS):
        value = 1.5
    elif any(word.startswith(stem) for stem in SOUND_SIGNAL):
        value = 0.65
    elif any(word.startswith(stem) for stem in AMBIGUOUS):
        nearby = text.lower()
        cue = any(stem in nearby for stem in OPTICS + SOUND_SIGNAL)
        value = 0.8 if cue else 0.0
    elif any(word.startswith(stem) for stem in BROAD_PHYSICS):
        value = 0.3
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return (doc, text), float(value)

"""Indentation detector for layers.0.mlp.down_proj:3203.

The component fires on a token made only of spaces and tabs, i.e. the leading
indentation of a line of code or text, and it is silent on ordinary words.
Its size depends on how wide that indentation is, counting a tab as 4 columns:

  7-10 columns    about 0.5   (light indent)
  11-19 columns   about 1.4   (the strongest: typical 3-4 level code indent)
  20-23 columns   about 0.8
  24-28 columns   about 0.1
  29+ columns     slightly negative

Anything else (ordinary text, punctuation, short 1-6 column runs) predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

# (lowest width, highest width, activation) in indentation columns.
BANDS = [
    (7, 10, 0.47),
    (11, 19, 1.37),
    (20, 23, 0.79),
    (24, 28, 0.12),
    (29, 33, -0.23),
    (34, 10**6, -0.36),
]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if not token or any(c not in " \t\xa0" for c in token):
        return carry, 0.0
    width = token.count(" ") + token.count("\xa0") + 4 * token.count("\t")
    for low, high, value in BANDS:
        if low <= width <= high:
            return carry, value
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 0, MLP down-projection, component 3204.

What it responds to, in plain terms:

* The first token of each document (no preceding context). Here the component is
  strongly signed by the token itself:
  - positive (about +0.3) when the token opens a sentence or heading: "The", "This",
    "A", "In", "How", "What", "It", ..., or a markdown/code opener starting with "#";
  - negative (about -0.25) for everything else: spaces, punctuation, digits,
    lowercase word fragments, capital letters that begin names or abbreviations, and
    special tokens.
* The second token of a document: slightly negative (about -0.04).
* Later tokens: near zero, except Chinese (Han) characters, which sit slightly above
  zero (about +0.035).

Documents are the runs of equal document ids in a packed row. Position counts from 0
at each document start, as the model's positions do.

Everything else is predicted as 0. The rules are coarse: they capture the
document-start response and the Han-character offset, not the many small
token-specific offsets that make up most of the remaining variance.
"""

READS = ()

# Words and symbols that commonly open a sentence, a heading or a code block.
OPENERS = frozenset(
    "The A This In It How What Why Is We When For There You If Are An Can Which "
    "Please Let Does These Do That Title Question By As".split()
)


def is_han(text):
    """True for a CJK unified ideograph (Chinese character)."""
    return bool(text) and 0x4E00 <= ord(text[0]) <= 0x9FFF


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or document != carry[0]:
        position = 0
    else:
        position = carry[1] + 1
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if position == 0:
        if token.startswith("#"):
            value = 0.33
        elif token in OPENERS:
            value = 0.3
        else:
            value = -0.25
    elif position == 1:
        value = -0.04
    elif is_han(token.strip()):
        value = 0.035
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return (document, position), value

    "satisfy satisfies satisfied inequality inequalities slope roots derivative".split()

    "angle matrix vector proof theorem sum sequence".split()

    'self': (0.426, 1.175, -0.806),

negative on multi-character Chinese/Japanese word chunks that open a grammatical
frame, i.e. a function word (在 in, 对 towards, 为 for, 是 is, 了, 等, 有, 让, 给, ...)
glued to the start of the phrase that must follow, such as 在全球, 对中国, 为主题,
是一个, 了一系列, 有不少. Weaker negatives: chunks opening with a Japanese particle
(を, が, は, と, に, る, て ...) and other 3+ character CJK chunks. Two-character
CJK chunks are near zero unless they open with such a function word. In code it
also goes negative on camel-case getter/setter/adder method pieces (.getName,
.setItems, .addObject) and on the token <tool_call>. Everything else is 0.

The activation is almost purely a function of the current token (within-token
variance is <1% for the 3+ character CJK chunks), so this program looks only at
the newest token's text. It does not track context or documents.

# Function words that open a grammatical frame in Chinese.
FRAME_WORDS = set("在等和了为是让给有要以如做没就对被把将从向到")
# Japanese particles / verb endings that open a frame in kana.
KANA_PARTICLES = set("をがはとにるてらでもの")

ACCESSOR = re.compile(r"^\.?\s?(get|set|add)[A-Z]")


def is_cjk(text):
    """True if every character is a CJK ideograph or a kana."""
    return bool(text) and all(
        "぀" <= ch <= "ヿ" or "一" <= ch <= "鿿" for ch in text
    )

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]  # the newest token, decoded alone
    value = 0.0
    if is_cjk(token) and len(token) >= 3:
        if token[0] in FRAME_WORDS:
            value = -1.6

            value = -0.6
        else:

    elif is_cjk(token) and len(token) == 2:
        if token[0] in FRAME_WORDS:
            value = -0.28
        elif token[0] in KANA_PARTICLES:
            value = -0.2
    elif ACCESSOR.match(token):
        value = -0.75
    elif token == "<tool_call>":
        value = -0.37
    return carry, float(value)
